title: bug: the compose-managed incumbent still carries every variable value in its docker inspect output
description:
Filed from task-0ca117e389df43ee9b458255f0752842, whose architect invited the filing rather than the widening.

THE ASYMMETRY. That row made the deployed CANDIDATE receive its environment through a bind-mounted file specifically so no value lands in `docker inspect .Config.Env` — measured: `--env` gives 1 grep hit for a planted value, a mounted file gives 0. The INCUMBENT is unchanged and is not held to that standard: `docker-compose.override.yml` delivers `DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:?set DATABASE_URL in .env}` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` to the compose `app` and `db` services, so the same values sit in THEIR `Config.Env` and are printed by `docker inspect` to anyone who can reach the docker socket.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE TODAY. `tests/e2e/foundation/platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts` sweeps `docker inspect <candidate>` (:218) and never sweeps the incumbent or the db container. So its `hits=0` result — and any epic claim resting on it that "no secret surfaces anywhere along the pipeline" — is true of the CANDIDATE only. The sweep is not wrong; its scope is just narrower than the sentence it is quoted for.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not prescribed: either extend the canary's sweep to the compose-managed containers and make the generated compose topology deliver by mounted file too, or narrow the epic's DoD-5 wording to say explicitly which containers were swept. Do NOT weaken the existing candidate sweep either way.

Not urgent: `.env` is already gitignored and excluded from every build context, so this is a local-socket exposure rather than a committed or published one. LOW.
definitionOfDone: Either the compose-managed app and db containers stop carrying variable values in docker inspect, or the epic's secrecy claim states in writing which containers the canary sweeps and which it does not.
The candidate-inspect sweep at platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts:218 is unchanged or strengthened, never narrowed.
If the sweep is extended, its swept=N count line rises and the new artifacts are named in the assertion message, as every other sweep in that file already is.

Proof it already holds live: the base compose the leaf landed HAS a top-level `secrets:` block, and :310 `expect(new Set(merged.keys())).toEqual(new Set(["app","db","proxy"]))` is green at HEAD. No parser fix needed; step 3 will add an explicit arm pinning it so it cannot silently regress.

MEASURED — THE ENTRYPOINT TRAP, live, on a real built product image (`moecanaryeafdb4b2-app:latest`, left by an earlier canary run), read exactly the way `imageCommandArgv` (deploy-candidate-environment.ts:148) does:
  docker image inspect --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}\n{{json .Config.Cmd}}'
  ["docker-entrypoint.sh"]
  ["node","/app/dist/server.js"]
So the node base image DOES contribute `docker-entrypoint.sh` even though the generated Dockerfile sets none. THE DESIGN ANSWER: set `command:` ONLY and never `entrypoint:`. `command:` replaces `.Config.Cmd` and LEAVES `.Config.Entrypoint` intact, so docker-entrypoint.sh needs no restoring and the trap is avoided by construction rather than worked around. (node's docker-entrypoint.sh prepends `node` only when $1 starts with `-` or is not on PATH; `/bin/sh` is neither, so it `exec "$@"`s our loader unchanged.) Step 3 will land this as an assertion pair — the override emits no `entrypoint:` key, and its `command:` is derived from DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH — rather than a comment.

MEASURED — COMPOSE INTERPOLATION WILL EAT THE LOADER unless escaped. Compose interpolates `$VAR`/`${VAR}` in the compose file and reports `invalid interpolation format` on a bare `$` before `(`. So the emitted loader must write `$$` for every literal `$`: `export DATABASE_URL="$$(cat /run/secrets/database_url)"`. Using `command:` only means the loader needs no `$0`/`$@` at all (it execs the entry path directly), so there is exactly ONE escape to get right instead of three. Verified live in step 5.

implementationPlan.description: Stop the app service delivering DATABASE_URL through compose `environment:`, in deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts. Replace that one line with a compose SECRET whose value still comes from `.env`, plus an entrypoint that loads it — the same shape the deployed candidate already uses, so the two paths stop disagreeing about what a secret is. Target shape: the app service keeps `PORT` in `environment:` (a port is not a secret), gains `secrets: [database_url]`, and a top-level `secrets: { database_url: { environment: DATABASE_URL } }` block. THE ENTRYPOINT TRAP, and it is the same one the candidate hit: setting `entrypoint:` in compose CLEARS the image's command, exactly as `--entrypoint` clears `.Config.Cmd`, so the service MUST also name `command:` explicitly or it starts with nothing to exec. Derive that `command:` from the `DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH` constant already in this file rather than retyping the path, so the Dockerfile's `CMD` and the override cannot drift apart. MEASURE, do not assume, whether the node base image's own `docker-entrypoint.sh` must be restored ahead of it — read the built image's `Entrypoint ++ Cmd` with `docker image inspect` the way `imageCommandArgv` does, and make the answer an assertion rather than a comment. The loader itself must put NO value in any argv: `export DATABASE_URL="$(cat /run/secrets/database_url)"; exec "$0" "$@"` names a path only. PRESERVE THE FAIL-FAST: `${DATABASE_URL:?set DATABASE_URL in .env}` makes compose refuse with a readable message today, and `secrets.environment` takes no `:?` form, so an unset variable would silently start the app with an empty connection string. Keep an equivalent and prove it with an arm.

DESIGN DECISION, AND IT DEPARTS FROM THE STEP TEXT — `command:` ONLY, NO `entrypoint:`. The step prescribed "an entrypoint that loads it" plus an explicit `command:`. Measured on a real built product image left by an earlier canary run (`moecanaryeafdb4b2-app:latest`), read exactly as `imageCommandArgv` does:
  docker image inspect --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}\n{{json .Config.Cmd}}'
  ["docker-entrypoint.sh"]
  ["node","/app/dist/server.js"]
So the trap is real. But `command:` replaces `.Config.Cmd` and LEAVES `.Config.Entrypoint` ALONE, which avoids the trap by construction instead of working around it: docker-entrypoint.sh needs no restoring, and the "must the base image's own entrypoint be restored ahead of it" question the step asked me to measure is answered NO, because nothing clears it. Confirmed on a live container below: `.Config.Entrypoint` came back `["docker-entrypoint.sh"]` with the override in force. Second benefit — the loader needs no `$0`/`$@`, so there is ONE `$` to escape rather than three. The step's stated invariant (no value in any argv, entry path derived from DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH not retyped) is fully honoured: `DATABASE_URL_LOADER` interpolates `DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH` and the new `DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_SECRET_PATH`.

FIVE LIVE MEASUREMENTS, all on docker 29.6.2 / compose v5.3.1, throwaway compose projects, all torn down (`docker ps -a | grep -c secretprobe` = none left, temp dirs rm -rf'd):

1. THE VALUE REACHES THE PROCESS. Value `postgres://app:probe-value-xyz@db:5432/app` (42 chars) in the compose environment, service `user: node`, loader as emitted. Container printed `LOADED_LEN=42` read back out of `process.env.DATABASE_URL` by node itself. Delivery is real, not assumed.

2. THE SECRET FILE IS READABLE BY THE UNPRIVILEGED USER — the risk that would have shown up as a mystery crash, since the generated Dockerfile ends `USER node`. `ls -l /run/secrets/database_url` inside the container: `-r--r--r-- 1 root root 42`, and `id` = `uid=1000(node) gid=1000(node)`. 4. `docker compose config` GREPPED FOR THE VALUE = 0; it resolves the secrets block to `environment: DATABASE_URL` — the NAME. This closes the "inspect is wider than Config.Env / compose config interpolates" risk the plan flagged.

5. FAIL-FAST PRESERVED, both branches, and it is BETTER than `:?` was because it refuses the whole project before any container is created:
     DATABASE_URL unset -> `secret "DATABASE_URL" must declare either `file` or `environment`: invalid compose project`
     DATABASE_URL=''    -> the same refusal
   The message names the variable and never a value. `:+` emits the NAME only when set-and-non-empty, so an empty source is what compose sees and rejects. A silently blank connection string is unreachable. This is the same idiom the leaf landed for POSTGRES_PASSWORD, so the two services now agree.

STRUCTURAL ARMS AT :306-322 NEEDED NO REPAIR, and that is a MEASUREMENT, not a hope: `composeServices` does not read a top-level `secrets:` key as a service, because it resets `inServices` on ANY column-0 key. All of `merged.keys() == {app,db,proxy}`, `composeServices(override).keys() == {app,proxy}`, `not.toContain("postgres")` and `not.toContain("\nvolumes:")` stayed green untouched. So neither the parser nor the assertion was "fixed" to accommodate the new key. I ADDED one line to that arm — `expect(override).toContain("\nsecrets:\n")` — so the property is pinned deliberately instead of holding by accident: without it, a parser change that started reading `secrets:` children as services would invent a fourth service and only the golden would notice.

NEW ARM 1 (pure, always runs) — "delivers the app's connection string as a secret, so no value reaches container metadata":
- BIDIRECTIONAL / UNIFORM, and this is the part that answers the bug report's own diagnosis. It iterates the MERGED project — `composeServices(base)` from the leaf's real `docker-compose.yml` producer PLUS `composeServices(override)` — and for EVERY service asserts its `environment:` block carries no `PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN|DATABASE_URL` line, allowing only `*_FILE:` entries whose value is under the derived `/run/secrets` root. Checking only the override is exactly how this leak survived its own canary sweep, so the arm covers both halves and names the offending service in the failure message.
- New helper `serviceSection(body, "    environment:")` reads only the lines under ONE 4-space key and stops at the next key at that depth. Reading the whole service body instead would let a value that moved from `environment:` into `secrets:` keep satisfying an "is it under environment" check — i.e. the arm would go vacuous the moment the fix landed.
- `SECRETS_MOUNT_ROOT` is DERIVED by slicing `DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_SECRET_PATH`, not retyped, so no arm can pin a mount root the generator stopped using.
- Sourcing: pins the exact `\nsecrets:\n  DATABASE_URL:\n    environment: ${DATABASE_URL:+DATABASE_URL}\n` block and the service's `- source:`/`target:` pair.
- THE SILENT REGRESSION IS NAMED AND EXCLUDED: `not.toContain("${DATABASE_URL}")` and `not.toContain("DATABASE_URL:?")`. A bare `${DATABASE_URL}` mounts an empty value and starts the app on a blank connection string while every byte golden in the file passes.
- THE ENTRYPOINT TRAP IS NOW AN ASSERTION, which is what step 2 asked for: `expect(override).not.toMatch(/^ {4}entrypoint:/mu)`. Anchored on a YAML KEY at service depth on purpose — the first version used `not.toContain("entrypoint:")` and WENT RED against correct code, because the emitted file's own comment names `entrypoint:` to explain why it is absent. That red is itself a small non-vacuity proof: the arm reads the real emitted bytes.
- DRIFT PIN, one constant across two generators: `command` must contain `exec node ${DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH}` AND the Dockerfile must contain `CMD ["node", "${DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH}"]`, so the override and the image cannot disagree about what to start.
- ESCAPE PIN: `command` must contain `"$$(cat ${DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_SECRET_PATH})\"`, and `command.replaceAll("$$","")` must contain no `$` — so a single-`$` regression (which compose rejects with "invalid interpolation format" before any container exists) is caught in the unit lane instead of in a live gate.

NEW ARM 2 (live, `it.runIf`) — "refuses the whole project when DATABASE_URL is unset or empty, naming the variable". THIS IS THE ARM STEP 2 DEMANDED for the fail-fast, and it had to be live: the secrets block has no `:?` form, so losing the fail-fast is SILENT and every byte golden passes either way. implementationPlan.description: Extend the canary's sweep to the compose-managed containers — DoD 1's measurement half and DoD 3. Today `sweeps` at :210-230 covers the CANDIDATE's inspect and logs, the proxy's Caddyfile, the receipts, the ledger and every generated and committed file, but never the compose `app` or `db` containers, which is why the leak was invisible. Add, each as its own labelled Sweep so the failure message names it: the app container's inspected configuration, the app container's logs, the db container's inspected configuration, the db container's logs, and the proxy container's inspected configuration. Resolve those container names the way the file already does — `docker ps --filter label=com.docker.compose.service=<name> --filter network=<project>_default --format {{.Names}}`, the pattern at :155 for db and :220 for proxy. THE EXISTING CANDIDATE SWEEP IS UNCHANGED AND UNNARROWED (DoD 2): add to the array, never edit or remove an entry. THIS ARM IS THE PROOF THE FIX WORKS AND IT MUST BE SHOWN TO FAIL FIRST: the canary is planted AS the postgres password (`PGPASSWORD=${CANARY}` at :158), so a db-inspect sweep goes RED against today's code. Run it once against the pre-fix templates, quote the failing labels, then confirm it goes green with the fix — a sweep added after the fix that was never seen red proves nothing. Update the `swept=N artifacts` line so N rises, and rewrite the file header's claim that no secret surfaces "ANYWHERE ALONG THE PIPELINE" to say what is now actually swept; that sentence was true of the candidate only and is the wording DoD 1 offers as the alternative branch.

LIVE RUN AND VERIFICATION. Acquire `full-suite-gate` and announce GATE START — these files stand up the generated topology verbatim and publish the product's real host ports (3000 and 5432), so two at once lose the bind. Run each leg standalone in the FOREGROUND, no pipes and no `;` chains, since a piped run reports tail's exit code. Legs: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, then the three `MOE_PLATFORM_PIPELINE=1` e2e files ONE AT A TIME with `--no-file-parallelism` — platform-secret-canary, platform-pipeline, platform-teardown-failure-paths. Quote each command, exit code and `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line is UNVERIFIED. Quote the canary's own `SECRET CANARY shape=... swept=N artifacts, hits=0` line with the RAISED N, and the pre-fix red from step 4 alongside it so the arm's non-vacuity is on the record. Also run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` if the leaf's version bump is in the same working tree, since the two profile-version mirrors live under apps/control-room and are invisible to the daemon leg (epic rail 1). Apply the path-attributed baseline for any repo-wide red: failing paths at the merge-base versus HEAD, delta intersected with this row's three owned paths must be EMPTY, foreign red quoted verbatim. TEARDOWN IS PART OF THE RUN: `composeDown` and the container removals must leave nothing behind on every exit path including the failure ones, and end with a `docker ps -a` census — epic rail 4 makes a leaked container or a held port inadmissible for every later gate on this board. Release the gate and announce GATE END.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then complete. Read the diff as an attacker. Specific questions this change earns: does the value reach `docker inspect` through any field other than `.Config.Env` — `.Config.Cmd`, `.Config.Entrypoint`, `.Config.Labels`, or the compose config hash label docker writes on every compose container? Does `docker compose config` print the resolved secret? Does the app's stdout log the connection string on a failed connect, and is that path actually exercised by the sweep or only the happy one? What happens on `docker compose up` with DATABASE_URL unset — a readable refusal, or an app that starts with an empty string and fails obscurely later? Is the new sweep falsifiable: mutate the app template back to `environment: DATABASE_URL` and confirm the canary goes RED naming the app container, then restore. RESTORE PROOF: back the mutated template out of tree to `%TEMP%/moe-task-9255156954-<basename>-<workerId>` — the task id in the path is mandatory, seat ids are reused across relaunches and a seat-keyed backup has held a stale vintage on this host — hash the LIVE file at window-open, and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Do the drill with NO full-suite lease held. Then confirm each of the three DoD items maps to a landed assertion, report all three touched paths in complete_step.modifiedFiles, and complete. Put the gate table in a task COMMENT first — completionSummary truncates silently at 2000 chars mid-word.
